title: The Sixteenth Homecoming
premise: Oscar Ravensworth is the anonymous coder behind 'Sixteenth Homecoming,' a leak account that has quietly exposed the rot beneath Millbrook's beloved founding tradition — a pageant that crowns one student each year while burying the town's ugliest secrets. When his civics teacher pairs him with Priya Chandrasekaran, the ambitious editor who has spent two years hunting his identity, Oscar must protect both his anonymity and the evidence he's gathered about the Homecoming Council's corruption, even as the council closes in on him. The semester becomes a cat-and-mouse game in which loyalty to his best friend Theo — whose family built the tradition — collides with the truth he owes everyone else. In the end, Oscar chooses truth over safety: he unmasks himself at the sixteenth homecoming itself, the council falls, the tradition survives only by being rebuilt honestly, and Oscar learns that justice outside the law still demands everything you are.
about_author: Ivo Halloran is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who covered three decades of high school pageants before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse office where the town's old parade banners hang like confessions on the wall.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. We meet Oscar mid-post: his anonymous account 'Sixteenth Homecoming' drops its first breadcrumb about the council's rigged voting system while he sits unnoticed in AP Computer Science. Establishes his rules for staying invisible and his fear when a post gets 40,000 views overnight. Emotional beat: the thrill of power warring with terror of exposure.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Collects Bylines
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya Chandrasekaran, editor of the school paper, has a corkboard of clues about the anonymous leaker and a scholarship riding on breaking the story. She narrows suspects to eleven students. Meanwhile her mother warns her off the Homecoming Council entirely. Emotional beat: ambition sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Mr. Okafor announces the semester capstone: document an institution's civic health, in pairs. He reads names aloud — Ravensworth and Chandrasekaran. The class laughs; nemesis with nemesis. Oscar's first task is surviving proximity to the one person hunting him. Emotional beat: dread disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Ground Rules
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Oscar and Priya negotiate terms in the library: no personal questions, equal credit, meetings in public. Both lie. Priya notices Oscar flinches at the word 'anonymous'; Oscar notices she keeps a photo of the council on her phone. Emotional beat: wary chess between two people who need each other's weaknesses.

chapters.title: Theo's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Best friend Theo Marsh reveals his family has chaired the Homecoming Council for four generations, and this year Theo will be inducted — the youngest ever. He asks Oscar to build the council's new digital voting app. Oscar realizes his own code may soon sit inside the machine he's been exposing. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Digging the capstone archive, Priya finds a 1970s ledger showing the council once expelled a student to protect a donor's son — and paid the family off. She doesn't yet connect it to Oscar, but she starts asking older townspeople questions, and someone reports her to the council. Emotional beat: the first taste of real danger.

chapters.title: The App Build
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar builds Theo's voting app and quietly installs a backdoor — not to rig it, but to watch it. He sees live proof that council chair Douglas Marsh (Theo's father) can override any vote. Oscar now holds evidence that indicts his best friend's father. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Coffee, Two Straws
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A council 'mentor' offers Priya an exclusive interview — clearly a bribe to steer her story. She records the offer secretly. That night she cross-references the ledger names and finds a Marsh signature from 1974. Emotional beat: temptation refused, and the intoxicating click of pieces aligning.

chapters.title: Fifteen Crowns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Research montage for the capstone: Oscar and Priya interview past 'homecoming royalty,' including a woman who says the crown ruined her life and another who calls it the best thing that ever happened here. The tradition is both beautiful and rotten, and neither teen can say which dominates. Emotional beat: doubt — the case isn't as clean as either wanted.

chapters.title: Slip
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Under deadline stress, Oscar references a detail from his own leaked post aloud. Priya says nothing, but that night she adds a twelfth name to her corkboard and underlines it twice. She begins engineering situations to test him. Emotional beat: hunter's patience; the reader feels the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Induction
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Theo is formally inducted into the council in a candlelit ceremony in the old grange hall. Oscar attends as his guest and witnesses Douglas Marsh instruct members to 'handle' a nosy reporter — meaning Priya. Oscar must decide whether to warn the person trying to unmask him. Emotional beat: loyalty inverted; protecting your enemy because it's right.

chapters.title: Anonymous Tip
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. An unsigned message warns Priya the council plans to get her suspended via a fabricated plagiarism claim. She suspects it's bait from Oscar to gauge her sources — or a genuine warning from inside. She publishes nothing but changes her tactics, going to the county records office instead. Emotional beat: paranoia as a way of life.

chapters.title: Midterm Collapse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Capstone midterm presentation goes badly: their partnership's contradictions show, Mr. Okafor threatens to split them up, and Theo — hurt that Oscar keeps vanishing — picks a fight. All three relationships strain simultaneously. Emotional beat: everything Oscar built to stay hidden begins crumbling at once.

chapters.title: The Backdoor Breach
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Douglas discovers anomalous traffic in the voting app and traces it toward a school IP address. A council tech contractor starts sweeping student devices. Oscar scrubs his hardware in a panic and realizes the account's next post may be his last chance to control the narrative. Emotional beat: cold sweat; the hunter has become prey.

chapters.title: Cornered in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Oscar in the library basement with her full file: timeline, IP patterns, the slip. She offers a deal — joint byline, his sources protected, the story published together. Oscar denies everything badly, then stops denying. Emotional beat: the relief of being known, tangled with the fear of what being known costs.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Story
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Forced alliance: Oscar shows Priya the backdoor logs proving vote manipulation across three years. But the logs also show Theo's induction vote was overridden — Theo won fairly and was cheated too. Telling the truth will destroy Theo's faith in his father and possibly in Oscar. Emotional beat: the price of honesty made concrete.

chapters.title: What Theo Deserves
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya argues they publish before homecoming night; Oscar argues they give Theo twenty-four hours to hear it from them first. Their argument becomes the book's thematic core: does justice served fast beat justice served whole? They compromise on a deadline — publish at noon Friday, homecoming is Saturday. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar tells Theo everything: the account, the backdoor, the logs. Theo's response is worse than anger — he defends his father, calls Oscar a traitor to the only family that ever treated him like one, and walks out. Then, alone, Theo opens the app and watches his own victory get overwritten. Emotional beat: heartbreak as the hinge of the plot.

chapters.title: Friday, Noon
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Publication day. The council's lawyer threatens injunctions; the principal pulls Priya's press credentials; Douglas Marsh implies Theo's college fund depends on silence. At 11:58 the site hosting their story mysteriously goes down — sabotage. Priya hits send anyway through a mirror server Oscar prepared. Emotional beat: defiance at the edge of ruin.

chapters.title: The Sixteenth Homecoming
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Saturday night. Half the town boycotts; half shows up angrier than ever. During the crowning ceremony, Oscar takes the microphone, unmasks himself as Sixteenth Homecoming, and reads the override logs aloud as Douglas moves toward the stage. Theo steps between them — not to stop Oscar, but to stop his father. Emotional beat: climax; courage as a public, irreversible act.

chapters.title: After the Crown
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Fallout: Douglas resigns under investigation, the state audits the council, Mr. Okafor gives their capstone an A with a note — 'truth is the assignment.' The tradition survives by reform: open votes, public ledgers, elected student co-chairs. Priya and Oscar publish a follow-up crediting every source, including Theo. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned hope.

chapters.title: Seventeenth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. One year later: Theo co-chairs the reformed council, Priya leaves for a journalism program, and Oscar archives the account — its work done — but keeps the login as a reminder. At the seventeenth homecoming, a new student asks him if the tradition is worth saving. He says: only if it belongs to everyone. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; justice as ongoing work, not a single act.
